text:
incbot: :rotating_light: PAGING: p99 latency breach on /v1/streaming/generate — threshold 10s, observed 12.4s. paging oncall (maria)

maria: on it. seeing alerts for p95/p99 spike. hit rate increased ~3x for streaming endpoints, tail latency clearly worse. starting triage.

raj: quick question — any recent deploys to preproc or template service? also will check tokenizer queue stats.

elinor: dashboards https://redwood.internal/d/streams/latency — snapshots below (pulled at 1976543220):
```
p50: 0.12s
p95: 1.85s (baseline ~0.25s)
p99: 8.6s (baseline ~0.9s)
tail (99.9): 18.2s
streaming stall rate (>3s): 12.3% of active streams
preproc queue depth: avg 42 -> spike to 420
mean prompt-expansion: 2.4s (up from 0.15s)
```

maria: ugh, prompt-expansion and preproc queue are the suspects. any errors in logs for the tokenizer?

raj: digging logs now. grep shows repeated retries for parsing tool schemas in JSON-mode, lots of expensive schema validation for incoming tool calls. sample log: `parse_tool_schema took 1640ms for request id=xyz` repeated across many requests. also seeing GC pauses on preproc pods.

devon: I pushed a change earlier today that allowed richer tool schemas to be parsed at preproc time (rollout at ~1976542000). commit: 7b9c4f2. It swaps deferred-schema-parse -> eager-parse for safety but that could be CPU-heavy.

maria: that matches. can we toggle back to deferred parsing? we need mitigation asap.

devon: will roll back the eager-parse flag and flip a config for json-mode heavy customers. doing `kubectl set env deployment/preproc EAGER_SCHEMA_PARSE=false --namespace=inference` now.

elinor: also recommend temporarily disabling JSON-mode for customers on dedicated paths that are causing most load — we can fallback to plain streaming (less validation). liz-cs can you confirm any affected customers?

liz-cs: two enterprise customers (acme and beta-inc) reported aborted sessions and timeouts in CS tickets. both are heavy tool-schema users and were migrated to JSON-mode last week. they've been escalated.

maria: plan: (1) rollback eager parse flag (devon) (2) flip per-customer config to disable JSON-mode for acme/beta-inc (devon) (3) increase preproc replica count by +3 to absorb backlog (ops-bot) (4) monitor p95/p99 and streaming stalls for 30m; if not improved, rollback the template rollout entirely.

devon: rollback applied: `kubectl set env deployment/preproc EAGER_SCHEMA_PARSE=false --namespace=inference` -> rollout started (rs: preproc-7c9bd). also ran: `kubectl patch customer/acme -p '{"spec":{"jsonMode":false}}'` and same for beta-inc.

ops-bot: `kubectl scale deploy/preproc --replicas=8 -n inference` executed.

raj: after the flag flip, preproc CPU on the set dropped by ~45% within 40s. queue depth down from 420 -> 70. first numbers coming in: p95 1.2s, p99 3.4s.

maria: great. keep those metrics streaming. any streaming stalls still visible?

elinor: stall rate down to 3.1% now. tail still noisy but trending down.

devon: we should also add a quick hotfix to bypass schema validation for streaming endpoints when responses are time-sensitive — minimal parsing fallback. will open a small patch but won't roll out until after stability.

maria: agree. action items captured. I'll take the incident bridge and handoff to elinor after my oncall window ends in 30m. elinor, you take second-watch and work with devon for the patch?

elinor: yes, will own the follow-up and watch metrics. please document timeline.

maria: short customer impact note for ops page: customers ACME and BETA-INC experienced increased latency and aborted streams ~1976542000-1976543260. we applied config flips and scaling; service returned to acceptable SLOs (p99 < 5s) at ~1976543255.

liz-cs: notifying ACME support contact with summary and that we disabled JSON-mode temporarily. will coordinate postmortem with them.

devon: commands used during mitigation: 
```
kubectl set env deployment/preproc EAGER_SCHEMA_PARSE=false -n inference
kubectl patch customer/acme -p '{"spec":{"jsonMode":false}}'
kubectl scale deploy/preproc --replicas=8 -n inference
curl -sS http://preproc-metrics:9090/metrics | grep prompt_expansion_latency
```

maria: nice. monitoring notes: keep an eye on GC and CPU hotspots in preproc. devs, add a light-weight schema cache + rate-limit expensive parses per-customer as medium-term fix.

elinor: creating internal incident ticket and assigning follow-ups: - rollback validation flag? (devon) - add schema cache (raj) - per-customer rate-limiter (devon/raj) - postmortem & customer timelines (liz-cs)

ops-bot: incidentbot created incident/INC-1976543210 with priority P1.

maria: handing off to elinor now. I'll be reachable but switching to read-only for the next 30m. thanks team. :pray:

elinor: taking over. will post updates to the incident doc and ping if anything regresses.

incbot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: p99s stabilized below 4.8s, streaming stall rate <4%, preproc queue normal. incident closed at 1976543268.
